rows.description: A stressed student who schedules an hour of football, dance or board games finds the mind returns sharper. Play is not wasted time but a recovery tool that adults often forget they need.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult notices friends treat every hobby as a side hustle or a metric. Doing something badly and purely for fun has become rare, and reclaiming it protects against burnout.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A child declares that there is nothing to do and clings to a parent. Boredom is a signal that the mind wants to generate its own activity, but the child does not yet know how.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Left without screens on a long summer afternoon, a child builds a fort, invents a game or draws for hours. Tolerated boredom is where self-directed interest first grows.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A parent instantly supplies a tablet whenever a child complains of boredom. The habit is kind but teaches that discomfort must be filled externally, and a short unrescued wait often yields creativity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager scrolls compulsively, switching apps to escape a flat feeling. The boredom is less about lack of options and more about intolerance for an empty moment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A student who feels bored in a course asks whether the material is too easy, too hard or simply meaningless to them. Reading boredom as data, not just a nuisance, guides better choices.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A toddler becomes clingy, tearful or wild when overtired, and cannot say why. Tiredness shows as behaviour, and a nap often solves what discipline cannot.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child fights bedtime, wanting one more story or fearing missing out. Predictable routines and calm endings teach that rest is safe and does not mean being left out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, calm, trust

rows.description: A child hears that resting is lazy while a busy adult is praised. Households that respect downtime raise children who can stop without shame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
